hints: Translate the first modulus inequality into its circle boundary, identifying its centre and radius before deciding which side is required.
For the comparison of distances from −2i and 2−4i, construct the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining those points.
Use one test point for each inequality to choose the permitted sides, then shade only the overlap and show whether each boundary is included.
walkthrough:
Interpret the first inequality $|z - (-2\mathrm{i})| \leqslant 3$ geometrically on the Argand diagram:
$$\text{Center: } C_1 = (0, -2) \quad (\text{representing } -2\mathrm{i})$$
$$\text{Radius: } R = 3$$
$$\text{The boundary is the circle } x^2 + (y + 2)^2 = 3^2 = 9, \text{ and the inequality represents the closed disk (interior and boundary).}$$

Interpret the second inequality $|z - (-2\mathrm{i})| \leqslant |z - (2 - 4\mathrm{i})|$ geometrically:
$$\text{Points representing the two base complex numbers: } A(0, -2) \text{ and } B(2, -4)$$
$$\text{Midpoint of } AB: \quad M = \left(\dfrac{0 + 2}{2}, \dfrac{-2 + (-4)}{2}\right) = (1, -3)$$

Determine the equation of the perpendicular bisector of segment $AB$:
$$\text{Gradient of } AB: \quad m_{AB} = \dfrac{-4 - (-2)}{2 - 0} = \dfrac{-2}{2} = -1$$
$$\text{Perpendicular gradient: } \quad m_{\perp} = -\dfrac{1}{-1} = +1$$
$$\text{Equation of the perpendicular bisector: } \quad y - (-3) = 1(x - 1) \implies y + 3 = x - 1 \implies y = x - 4$$

Determine which side of the perpendicular bisector is required:
$$\text{The condition } |z - A| \leqslant |z - B| \text{ means points closer to or equidistant from } A(0, -2) \text{ than } B(2, -4).$$
$$\text{Test } A(0, -2): \quad -2 \geqslant 0 - 4 = -4 \text{ (true), so the half-plane containing } A(0, -2) \text{ is } y \geqslant x - 4.$$

Conclude the shaded region:
$$\text{Shade the intersection of the solid closed disk } x^2 + (y + 2)^2 \leqslant 9 \text{ and the half-plane on the side of } y = x - 4 \text{ containing } (0, -2).$$

ai_rubric.Argand Loci: Demonstrates a circle centred at $(0,-2)$. The intersection of the closed disc centred at $(0,-2)$ with radius $3$ and the half-plane on the side of the perpendicular bisector through $(1,-3)$ that contains $(0,-2)$.
